title: GA/865/2001 of STATE Vs MEHBOOB and ORS.

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
GOVERNMENT APPEAL NO. 865/2001
Stateof Uttaranchal ......... Appellant
Versus
Mehboob & Others .......... Respondents
Mr. PS Danu, Advocate, for the State/appellant.
Mr. Vivek Shukla, Advocate, for the accused/respondents.
28h February, 2013
Hon'ble Servesh Kumar Gupta, J.
 This is a Government Appeal against the
judgment and order of acquittal dated 10.1.2001
rendered by the Additional Sessions Judge, Dehradun in
Sessions Trial No. 131/98, State v. Mehboob & Others.
2. There were four accused persons who were
named in the FIR and the chargesheet was submitted
against them for the offence of Section 308/504 IPC. One
of the accused Khalil is the father and rest of the
accused, namely, Mehboob, Liyakat and Mohd. Hanif are
his sons. It is pertinent to mention that one of the
accused Khalil has now died. Therefore, appeal in his
respect stands abated.
3. Initially the law was set into motion by lodging
the FIR on 1.6.1996 at 7.40 pm by Mehboob, father of
the injured Kurban (to remove the confusion, it deserves
mention that name of one of the accused is also
Mehboob). FIR was lodged for the offences under Section
324/506 IPC while chargesheet was submitted for graver
offences i.e. under Section 308/504 IPC. Obviously, the
gravity of the offence was adjudged by the Investigation
Officer considering the injury report of victim Kurban,
who has been examined as PW1 before the trial court.

2
4. It is also pertinent to mention that inured and
the accused persons were residing in the same are and in
close vicinity to each other, at the distance of few paces
only. In the backdrop of the incident, which occurred on
1.6.1996 at 5.30 pm, is that accused persons owed some
financial debt to the injured and his father and some
money of the informant was stolen. This dispute was
persisting. On the date of event, Kurban went to offer
Namaj prayers in the Mosque, which was nearer to the
house of the accused persons. After offering the prayers,
when he was coming back, he was allegedly confronted
by the accused persons, who assaulted him collectively.
Mehboob gave a blow of knife upon the body of Kurban,
Hanif allegedly gave blow of lathi, while rest of the
accused persons bate him with fists and kicks. Kurban
fell down on the earth. His body became blood soaked.
5. Noor Mohammad (PW3), an eyewitness,
informed about the incident to the father of injured, who
reached at the spot and carried him to Primary Health
Centre, Sahaspur, which was approximately four
kilometres away from the place of occurrence. However,
injured could not get treatment there and was referred to
Dehradun. So, he was admitted in Doon Hospital,
Dehradun by his brother Gulsher, while his father
Mehboob lodged the FIR Ex. Ka-1 after two hours and ten
minutes of the incident. Chick report is Ex. Ka-3. After
the investigation, chargesheet was submitted as stated
above. Charges were levelled against all the accused
persons for the offence of Section 308/34 and 504 IPC.
6. Prosecution has examined injured PW1
Kurban, PW2 Mehboob, informant and father of the

3
injured, PW3 Noor Mohammad, PW4 Mir Hasan, PW5
Furkan, PW6 Dr. AK Jain and PW7 Constable Santosh
Kumar, who wrote the chick report at the police station.
This Court has been apprised that since the Investigation
Officer of the case died during pendency of the trial,
formal papers were proved by PW7, who once was posted
with the Investigation Officer and had acquaintance with
his writing and signature.
7. It would be relevant to mention the injuries
found on the body of Kurban, as recorded in the injury
report Ex. Ka-2 prepared by Dr. AK Jain at Doon
Hospital, Dehradun on 1.6.1996 at 9.15 pm. The same
are as under:
 "(1) Incised wound 4 cm x 1.5 cm
muscle deep left side forehead 2 cm above left
eyebrow.
 (2) T/swelling 16 cm x 23 cm around
left forearm 4 cam below left elbow.
 (3) Lacerated wound 2 cm x 0.5 cm x
bone deep left forearm 10 cm below left elbow.
 (4) Abrasion 10 cm x 1 cm left side
back semicircular in shape.
 (5) Contusion 19 cam x 5 cm left side
chest 13 cm below left axilla.
 (6) Abrasion 7 cm x 2 cm top left
shoulder.
Opinion : Injury No. (1) (2) (3) (4) (5) (6) are
fresh. Injury No. (1) caused by sharp edged
object and rest by hard and blunt object. (1),
(2), (3), (5) kept under observation, rest are
simple in nature. Patient admitted."

4
8. Learned Counsel for the respondents
vehemently argued, which is also the main reason behind
acquittal, that the injured Kurban regained his
consciousness after 2-3 hours of the incident, while
another version in the cross-examination of his father
PW2 is that his son's consciousness returned on next day
i.e. on 2.6.1996, then how the report could be lodged
after two hours and ten minutes of the said incident
implicating the accused persons. This argument is not
tenable in view of this Court because it is amply clear
that the place of occurrence is 4 kilometres from the
concerned police station Sahaspur, where the FIR was
lodged, and the injured remained lying at the spot for
half an hour. Thereafter he was brought to the Primary
Health Centre, Sahaspur. Therefore, this two hours ten
minutes time could naturally be consumed in bringing
the injured to Sahaspur. It has nowhere come that he
was so unconscious as to unable to disclose the names of
assailants. Nature of injuries are also not so grave to
make him completely unconscious and unable to reveal
the names of the assailants. From the nature of injuries,
which injured Kurban suffered, at the most it can be
inferred that he might have been drifting in and out of
consciousness, and in all probabilities he must have
been this much consciousness so as to disclose the
names of the assailants during this two hours ten
minutes time.
9. Learned Counsel for the respondents accused
has vociferously contended that informant Mehboob
(PW2), father of injured, has disclosed that his son
regained consciousness on the next day of the occurrence
and even the injured himself (PW1) has admitted that his
consciousness returned after 2-3 hours of the incident.

5
So, if his consciousness returned after 2-3 hours, then
how he can disclose the names of the assailants and,
therefore, the accused persons have been falsely
implicated in the FIR, which was lodged after two hours
and ten minutes of the alleged incident before regaining
the consciousness by the injured.
10. As regards the father's statement that the
injured regained his consciousness on the next day of the
incident, this contradiction is not fatal to the case of
prosecution because PW2 Mehboob was examined after
three and half years of the incident and at that time he
was 70 years old. So, the memory of such a
septuagenarian person may slightly fade in the above
circumstances and he might cannot exactly recall each
and every details relating to the said incident, and that
too when he was being cross-examined at the hands of a
senior counsel in unusual surroundings of the
courtroom.
11. Dr. AK Jain (PW6), who examined the injured
at Doon Hospital, has disclosed in his cross-examination
that had the injured been unconscious, he would have
had mentioned this fact in the injury report prepared by
him. This statement of the doctor clearly suggests that
the injured became fully conscious much before he was
brought for the medical examination at Dehradun.
12. PW1 Kurban, the injured, has proved the case
and motive behind the occurrence. He is an illiterate
person and if there is any minor contradiction between
his statement and the statement of his father PW2, those
contradictions are not of such a magnitude as to
disbelieve the prosecution story as a whole. Where the

6
witnesses are illiterate and rustic poor persons being
examined at the hands of a senior counsel in the
courtroom, then such discrepancies and minor
contradictions are bound to occur. No criminal trial is
free from minor contradictions, but the court has to
weigh and judge such things taking into consideration
the circumstances in totality.
13. It was further contended that PW3 to PW5,
who are eyewitnesses of the incident, have not supported
the prosecution version and they have been declared
hostile. This argument also does not hold much water for
the reason that PW3 Noor Mohammad has partly
supported the prosecution version to the extent that he
was also returning after offering the Namaj prayer and
Kurban was coming behind him. He heard some
troubling voice from his behind, which was of Kurban. At
that relevant time, Kurban was in front of the house of
accused Mehboob. In the meantime, Kurban fell down at
the spot in almost unconsciousness. He gave the
information to the Kurban's house and thereafter with
the assistance of his father, he took the injured for
medical aid. He said that injured was assaulted by
Mehboob. However, he has said that he did not see any
other person at the spot.
14. PW4 Mir Hasan has also supported the
prosecution version partially to the extent that he was
also returning after offering Namaj at the relevant date,
time and place. He saw quarrelling Mehboob and Kurban
with each other, but he said that Mehboob was alone.
PW5 Furkan has also said that he saw Kurban lying by
the side of road.

7
15. It is settled principle of law, reiterated time
and again by the Hon'ble Apex Court, that testimony of a
hostile witness can be looked into to the extent it
supports the prosecution version. As such, there is no
force in the argument of learned Counsel for the accused
respondents.
16. PW5 Furkan, in his cross-examination, has
stated that he and family members of injured had taken
Kurban to hospital at Sahaspur where he could not be
medically examined. The disclosure of names by Kurban
to his father while being carried to the Primary Health
Centre, Sahaspur is also relevant and admissible in the
evidence.
17. From forgoing discussion of evidence, it is
clear that ocular version of the prosecution is well
corroborated by the medical evidence. Motive behind the
incident has also been indicated. Moreover, the injured
himself has been examined, who has supported the case
of prosecution and his testimony inspires confidence, and
there is no reason to disbelieve his statement.
Consequently, the impugned judgment and order of the
trial court is liable to be set aside.
18. For the reasons recorded above, I hold the
accused, namely, Mehboob, Liyakat and Mohd. Hanif
guilty of the offence punishable under Section 308/34
and 504 IPC as the case is proved beyond reasonable
doubt against the said accused persons. Appeal in
respect of Khalil, being died, has already been abated.
19. Resultantly, appeal is allowed. Impugned
judgment and order dated 10.1.2001, passed by the
Additional Sessions Judge, Dehradun in Sessions Trial

8
No. 131/98, State v. Mehboob & Others, is hereby set
aside. Mehboob, Liyakat and Mohd. Hanif are convicted
for the offences under Section 308/34 and 504 IPC.
20. On the quantum of sentence, learned Counsel
for the accused respondents pleaded mercy of this Court
and prayed that the convicts be let off only with the
sentence of fine because now they are living peacefully in
the same area in close vicinity after the occurrence and
incident took place about 16-17 years ago. This prayer
was opposed by the learned State Counsel, who stated
that keeping in view the injuries sustained by the injured
Kurban, all convicts deserve severe punishment.
21. Having considered the facts and circumstances
of the case as well as the submissions of learned Counsel
for the parties, each of the convicts is sentenced to
undergo one year's rigorous imprisonment along with fine
of rupees ten thousand each for the offence under
Section 308/34 IPC. In default of payment of fine, they
shall undergo three months' rigorous imprisonment. For
the offence of Section 504 IPC, each convict is awarded
fine of rupees five thousand, in default thereof they shall
undergo two months' rigorous imprisonment. The period
already spent by the convicts during investigation and
trial in connection with this crime shall be adjusted in
the above sentence imposed by this Court.
22. Let a copy of this judgment and order be sent
to the trial court for its compliance. Lower court record
be also sent back.
 (Servesh Kumar Gupta, J.)
28.2.2013
Prabodh
